why: Minimise the finishing time: if every process can be done when each processor runs at most k of them, it can with k + 1, so binary search k. The check is greedy, largest processes go to the largest processors, k at a time. A processor running k processes takes 2k - 1 seconds.
hints: A processor that runs k processes needs k seconds of work plus k - 1 pauses. So the question becomes: what is the smallest k that works?

Fix k. Sort processes and capacities descending; give the strongest processor the k largest processes, the next one the next k, and so on. If a process is larger than the processor it reaches, k fails. Feasibility is monotone in k.
If the largest process exceeds every capacity, return -1. Otherwise binary search k in [1, n] and return 2k - 1. O((n + m) log n).
constraints:
• 1 <= n, m <= 105
  • 1 <= processSize[i], capacity[i] <= 109
  • The source shows no bounds; these are practice assumptions.
